import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def bubble_sort_precond (v : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
def bubblePass : Int → List Int → List Int × Int
  | x, [] => ([], x)
  | x, y :: t =>
    if x ≤ y then (x :: (bubblePass y t).1, (bubblePass y t).2)
    else (y :: (bubblePass x t).1, (bubblePass x t).2)

lemma bubblePass_nil (x : Int) : bubblePass x [] = ([], x) := by
  simp [bubblePass]

lemma bubblePass_cons_le (x y : Int) (t : List Int) (h : x ≤ y) :
    bubblePass x (y :: t) = (x :: (bubblePass y t).1, (bubblePass y t).2) := by
  simp [bubblePass, h]

lemma bubblePass_cons_gt (x y : Int) (t : List Int) (h : ¬ x ≤ y) :
    bubblePass x (y :: t) = (y :: (bubblePass x t).1, (bubblePass x t).2) := by
  simp [bubblePass, h]

lemma pass_snd_nil (x : Int) : (bubblePass x []).2 = x := by
  rw [bubblePass_nil]

lemma pass_length (x : Int) (t : List Int) : (bubblePass x t).1.length = t.length := by
  induction t generalizing x with
  | nil => simp [bubblePass_nil]
  | cons y t ih =>
    rcases le_or_gt x y with h | h
    · rw [bubblePass_cons_le x y t h]
      simp [ih]
    · rw [bubblePass_cons_gt x y t (not_le.mpr h)]
      simp [ih]

lemma pass_perm (x : Int) (t : List Int) :
    ((bubblePass x t).1 ++ [(bubblePass x t).2]).Perm (x :: t) := by
  induction t generalizing x with
  | nil =>
    have h1 : (bubblePass x ([] : List Int)).1 ++ [(bubblePass x ([] : List Int)).2] = [x] := by
      simp [bubblePass_nil]
    rw [h1] <;> exact List.Perm.refl _
  | cons y t ih =>
    rcases le_or_gt x y with h | h
    · rw [bubblePass_cons_le x y t h]
      exact List.Perm.cons x (ih y)
    · rw [bubblePass_cons_gt x y t (not_le.mpr h)]
      exact List.Perm.trans (List.Perm.cons y (ih x)) (List.Perm.swap x y t)

lemma pass_le (x : Int) (t : List Int) : ∀ z ∈ x :: t, z ≤ (bubblePass x t).2 := by
  induction t generalizing x with
  | nil =>
    intro z hz
    simp at hz
    subst hz
    exact le_of_eq (pass_snd_nil _).symm
  | cons y t ih =>
    intro z hz
    rcases le_or_gt x y with h | h
    · rw [bubblePass_cons_le x y t h]
      have hy : y ≤ (bubblePass y t).2 := ih y y List.mem_cons_self
      simp only [List.mem_cons] at hz
      rcases hz with rfl | rfl | hz
      · exact le_trans h hy
      · exact hy
      · exact ih y z (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hz)
    · rw [bubblePass_cons_gt x y t (not_le.mpr h)]
      have hx : x ≤ (bubblePass x t).2 := ih x x List.mem_cons_self
      simp only [List.mem_cons] at hz
      rcases hz with rfl | rfl | hz
      · exact hx
      · exact le_trans (le_of_lt h) hx
      · exact ih x z (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hz)

lemma pairwise_snoc : ∀ (l : List Int) (b : Int), List.Pairwise (· ≤ ·) l →
    (∀ a ∈ l, a ≤ b) → List.Pairwise (· ≤ ·) (l ++ [b]) := by
  intro l b
  induction l with
  | nil => intro _ _; simp
  | cons x xs ih =>
    intro h hb
    rw [List.pairwise_cons] at h
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := h
    rw [List.cons_append, List.pairwise_cons]
    refine ⟨?_, ih h2 (fun a ha => hb a (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ ha))⟩
    intro c hc
    rcases List.mem_append.mp hc with hc | hc
    · exact h1 c hc
    · simp at hc
      subst hc
      exact hb x (by simp)

def bsAux : Nat → List Int → List Int
  | 0, l => l
  | _ + 1, [] => []
  | n + 1, x :: t => bsAux n (bubblePass x t).1 ++ [(bubblePass x t).2]
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definitions
def bubble_sort (v : List Int) (h_precond : bubble_sort_precond v) : List Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  bsAux v.length v
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def bubble_sort_postcond (v : List Int) (result : List Int) (h_precond : bubble_sort_precond v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) result ∧ result.Perm v
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
lemma bsAux_spec : ∀ (n : Nat) (l : List Int), l.length ≤ n →
    List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) (bsAux n l) ∧ (bsAux n l).Perm l := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    intro l hl
    have hl0 : l = [] := by
      cases l with
      | nil => rfl
      | cons x t => simp at hl
    subst hl0
    simp [bsAux]
  | succ n ih =>
    intro l hl
    cases l with
    | nil => simp [bsAux]
    | cons x t =>
      have hlen : (bubblePass x t).1.length ≤ n := by
        rw [pass_length]
        simp at hl
        omega
      obtain ⟨hs, hp⟩ := ih (bubblePass x t).1 hlen
      have hbs : bsAux (n + 1) (x :: t)
          = bsAux n (bubblePass x t).1 ++ [(bubblePass x t).2] := by
        simp [bsAux]
      rw [hbs]
      have hsorted : List.Pairwise (· ≤ ·)
          (bsAux n (bubblePass x t).1 ++ [(bubblePass x t).2]) := by
        refine pairwise_snoc _ _ hs ?_
        intro a ha
        exact pass_le x t a ((pass_perm x t).subset (List.mem_append_left _ (hp.subset ha)))
      exact ⟨hsorted, (hp.append_right _).trans (pass_perm x t)⟩
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem bubble_sort_postcond_satisfied (v : List Int) (h_precond : bubble_sort_precond v) :
    bubble_sort_postcond v (bubble_sort v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  exact bsAux_spec v.length v (le_refl _)
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## Analysis

**Implementation.** Bubble sort can be decomposed into a *pass* which walks the list swapping adjacent out‑of‑order elements. It is convenient to let the pass return a pair: the list of the first `n-1` elements after bubbling, together with the last element (which is the maximum that got "bubbled" to the end):

```
bubblePass x []      = ([], x)
bubblePass x (y::t)  = if x ≤ y then (x :: (bubblePass y t).1, (bubblePass y t).2)
                                else (y :: (bubblePass x t).1, (bubblePass x t).2)
```

This is structurally recursive on the list argument, so no termination proof is needed.

Then bubble sort repeats passes; each pass fixes the maximum at the end, so we recurse on the prefix. To keep everything structurally recursive I use a `Nat` fuel (instantiated with the list length):

```
bsAux 0       l       = l
bsAux (n+1)   []      = []
bsAux (n+1) (x::t)    = bsAux n (bubblePass x t).1 ++ [(bubblePass x t).2]
```

**Key lemmas about a pass** (all by induction on the list, generalizing the carried element):

* `pass_length` : `(bubblePass x t).1.length = t.length` (needed for the fuel bound).
* `pass_perm`   : `(bubblePass x t).1 ++ [(bubblePass x t).2] ~ x :: t`.
* `pass_le`     : every element of `x :: t` is `≤ (bubblePass x t).2` (so the extracted element is the maximum).

**Correctness of `bsAux`** by induction on the fuel `n`, for all `l` with `l.length ≤ n`:
the recursive call is on `(bubblePass x t).1` whose length equals `t.length ≤ n`, giving sortedness and permutation by IH; then `List.sorted_append` reduces sortedness of `bsAux n p.1 ++ [p.2]` to (i) sortedness of the recursive result, (ii) `[p.2]` sorted, (iii) every element of the result is `≤ p.2`, which follows from the permutation facts plus `pass_le`. The permutation part is `hp.append_right _ |>.trans (pass_perm x t)`.

    · rw [bubblePass_cons_le x y t h]
      exact List.Perm.cons x (ih y)
    · rw [bubblePass_cons_gt x y t (not_le.mpr h)]
      exact List.Perm.trans (List.Perm.cons y (ih x)) (List.Perm.swap x y t)

lemma pass_le (x : Int) (t : List Int) : ∀ z ∈ x :: t, z ≤ (bubblePass x t).2 := by
  induction t generalizing x with
  | nil =>
    intro z hz
    simp at hz
    subst hz
    exact le_of_eq (pass_snd_nil _).symm
  | cons y t ih =>
    intro z hz
    rcases le_or_gt x y with h | h
    · rw [bubblePass_cons_le x y t h]
      have hy : y ≤ (bubblePass y t).2 := ih y y List.mem_cons_self
      simp only [List.mem_cons] at hz
      rcases hz with rfl | rfl | hz
      · exact le_trans h hy
      · exact hy
      · exact ih y z (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hz)
    · rw [bubblePass_cons_gt x y t (not_le.mpr h)]
      have hx : x ≤ (bubblePass x t).2 := ih x x List.mem_cons_self
      simp only [List.mem_cons] at hz
      rcases hz with rfl | rfl | hz
      · exact hx
      · exact le_trans (le_of_lt h) hx

lemma pairwise_snoc : ∀ (l : List Int) (b : Int), List.Pairwise (· ≤ ·) l →
    (∀ a ∈ l, a ≤ b) → List.Pairwise (· ≤ ·) (l ++ [b]) := by
  intro l b

  | nil => intro _ _; simp
  | cons x xs ih =>
    intro h hb
    rw [List.pairwise_cons] at h
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := h
    rw [List.cons_append, List.pairwise_cons]

    intro c hc
    rcases List.mem_append.mp hc with hc | hc
    · exact h1 c hc
    · simp at hc
      subst hc
      exact hb x (by simp)

def bsAux : Nat → List Int → List Int

The student implements bubble sort from scratch using the expected adjacent-comparison logic:

- `bubblePass` traverses the list while carrying one element. At each step, it compares adjacent candidates `x` and `y`, emits the smaller one, and carries the larger one forward. Thus, one pass moves a maximum element to the end.
- `bsAux` repeatedly applies this pass, recursively sorting the pass’s prefix and appending the maximum element. With `v.length` iterations, this is the standard quadratic bubble-sort structure.
- `bubble_sort` invokes `bsAux v.length v`; it does not delegate sorting to a built-in or preverified sorting routine.
- The supporting lemmas establish preservation of length and elements, maximality of the carried element, sortedness, and permutation.
- There are no cheating constructs such as `sorry`, `admit`, axioms, empty placeholder implementations, or calls to an existing sorting function.

Although the recursive presentation completes each pass before recursively sorting the remaining prefix, it is semantically a standard bubble-sort implementation based on repeated adjacent swaps/comparisons and has the required O(N²) behavior.
